_notes:
Bosch BMM150 3-axis geomagnetic sensor at 0x10-0x13 (CSB and SDO pins; 0x13 with both high, the DFRobot board's default)
Detection: after power-up the chip is in suspend mode, where only the power control register (0x4B) works and every other register reads 0, so the chip ID can't be read until it is powered: 0x4B reads 0 or 1 (bits 7-1 0: the soft reset bits clear themselves and SPI 3-wire is off), then 0x4B = 0x01 (power control on, which is also the state the init leaves), 3 ms (start-up), then chip ID (0x40) = 0x32. Records are tried in order of detection strength, so at 0x10-0x13 the ones with a read-only ID (VEML7700, MXC400xXC) go before it and VEML6040 (no detection values) after it; the write reaches whatever passed the 0x4B check - for a VEML6040 an unused command code
Init: power control on (0x4B = 0x01), 3 ms; soft reset (0x4B = 0x83, keeping power on), 3 ms - the chip is then in sleep mode with its reset settings; repetitions as Bosch's regular preset: REP_XY (0x51) = 4 (9 repetitions), REP_Z (0x52) = 14 (15); OP mode (0x4C) = 0x00 - normal mode, 10 Hz
Poll (100 ms): data X, Y, Z and RHALL (0x42-0x49), then the trim registers (0x5D-0x71: dig_x1, dig_y1, dig_z4, dig_x2, dig_y2, dig_z2, dig_z1, dig_xyz1, dig_z3, dig_xy2, dig_xy1) - read every poll as the decode code has nowhere to keep them. X and Y are 13-bit and Z 15-bit two's complement, left-justified in their registers; RHALL 14-bit
Decode: Bosch's floating-point compensation (BMM150 Sensor API compensate_x, _y, _z), giving uT. valid is 0 when an axis reads its overflow value (X, Y -4096, Z -16384), RHALL is 0 (no measurement yet) or a trim needed is 0. No hard- or soft-iron correction: the board and its surroundings add their own offsets
Source: registers, modes and presets from the Bosch BMM150 datasheet (BST-BMM150-DS001); the compensation from Bosch's BMM150 Sensor API (https://github.com/boschsensortec/BMM150_SensorAPI, BSD-3-Clause)
